results.content: With three months to go until the U.S. midterm elections in November, voters increasingly seem to prefer Democrats over the Republican Party that has had control of Congress for the last two years. Results of a Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday showed that 42% of registered voters would vote for a Democratic congressional candidate at present, compared to 37% for a Republican. The same survey also found that, for the first time in nearly a decade of its polling series, voters perceive the Democratic Party as having a better plan for the economy than the Republican Party. results.content: President Donald Trump has broken his own record for the lowest approval rating recorded by The Economist/YouGov, with just 33 percent of Americans now saying they approve of the way he is handling his job as president. What To Know The significance of the latest result is ultimately less about one number than about the trajectory. Trump Hits New Lows Among Key Blocs Trump’s approval is also reaching new lows across several key voting blocs. Trump has a new net approval low among white Americans too, with a 39 percent approval in the new poll compared to 57 percent disapproval.
